title: Assemble the Report
content:
What problem does this solve?
A program often needs to combine fixed words with values that can change. An f-string lets Python build one readable string from both.

Start with the behavior
  name = "Ada"
  print(f"Hello, {name}")
The f before the opening quote tells Python to evaluate what appears inside { } and insert the result into the text.

You can insert more than one value
  item = "torch"
  count = 4
  print(f"{item}: {count}")

Vocabulary after the behavior
The f-string is one string value. The braces mark expressions Python should evaluate and place into that string.

Why this matters
If a stored value changes, the report can change with it. You do not need to rewrite the surrounding sentence by hand.
concepts: An f before the opening quote enables { } replacement fields
Names inside braces are evaluated and inserted into the string
Several changing values can be combined into one readable line

examples.title: One inserted value
examples.explanation: The value stored in name is inserted where {name} appears.

examples.title: Two values
examples.explanation: Both variables contribute to one output line.

examples.title: Expedition report
examples.explanation: The sentence stays readable while the data can change.

common_mistakes: Forgetting the f prefix and seeing {name} printed literally
Putting quotes around the variable name inside braces
Hardcoding the value into the sentence instead of using the stored variable

exercises.title: One inserted value
hints: Find the value stored in name first.
{name} is replaced by the current value of name.

exercises.title: Insert the count
exercises.prompt:
Change the expression inside the braces so the output is exactly:
Count: 3
hints: The value you need is already stored in count.
Replace the 0 inside { } with the variable name.

exercises.title: Two values
exercises.prompt:
The starter variables are already provided. Print exactly:
torch: 4

Use one f-string and both variables.
exercises.starter_code:
item = "torch"
count = 4

# Print one formatted line
hints: The fixed punctuation is just : and a space; the changing parts come from the variables.
Place item and count in separate { } fields inside one f-string.

tests.message: Use an f-string for the line.

exercises.title: Missing f
exercises.prompt: The program should print Status: READY, but it prints the braces literally. Repair the print line.
hints: The braces are currently inside an ordinary string.
Python only replaces {status} when the string is marked as an f-string.
Add f immediately before the opening quote.

exercises.title: Field Dispatch Card
exercises.prompt:
Build a four-line dispatch card from the supplied variables.

Required output:
EXPEDITION DISPATCH
Expedition: 17
Registered: 4
3 days overdue | OVERDUE

Requirements:
- keep the supplied variables
- include one useful # comment
- use the variables to build the changing report lines
- use f-strings for at least the report lines that combine labels or values

The point is that the report is assembled from stored data rather than copied as one fixed block of text.
exercises.starter_code:
expedition = 17
registered = 4
days_overdue = 3
status = "OVERDUE"

# Build the dispatch card below
exercises.reference_solution:
expedition = 17
registered = 4
days_overdue = 3
status = "OVERDUE"

# These lines are built from the stored expedition data
print("EXPEDITION DISPATCH")
print(f"Expedition: {expedition}")
print(f"Registered: {registered}")
print(f"{days_overdue} days overdue | {status}")
hints: Separate the fixed heading from the lines that depend on stored values.
Use expedition, registered, days_overdue, and status inside f-strings instead of typing their values again in the report lines.
A working structure is one heading print followed by three f-string prints built from the four variables, plus a # comment.

tests.message: Use f-strings to assemble the report from variables.

tests.expected:
EXPEDITION DISPATCH
Expedition: 17
Registered: 4
3 days overdue | OVERDUE

exercises.success_message: The dispatch is now assembled from stored data instead of being one hardcoded message.
